description: Three mystery babies in Fox's jars by the pond: a tadpole, a caterpillar and a bean seed. Robo guesses fish, snake and rock; Fox builds three life-cycle wheels (frog, butterfly, bean), opens a cutaway bean seed, and compares how each living thing starts, grows, makes young and repeats.

youtube.title: Life Cycles for Kids! Frog, Butterfly and Bean Plant | Grade 3 Science | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
Fox has three mystery babies in jars by the pond: a wriggly tadpole, a stripy caterpillar and a bean seed. Robo guesses a baby fish, a baby snake and a little rock... not even close!
Build three life-cycle wheels and watch each one grow: frog (egg, tadpole, tadpole with legs, froglet, adult frog), butterfly (egg, caterpillar or larva, chrysalis or pupa, adult: complete metamorphosis) and bean plant (seed, sprout, young plant, flowers, pods with new seeds). Open a bean seed to see the seed coat, the tiny baby plant and its stored food, find out why a chrysalis is not a cocoon, and compare what all life cycles share: start life, grow, make young, and the cycle goes round again.
For third graders (NGSS 3-LS1-1).

Try at home with a grown-up: fold a wet paper towel inside a clear jar, slide a dried bean between the towel and the glass, keep it damp and warm, and watch which comes out first, the root or the shoot. Wash your hands after touching soil, seeds or pond water, don't eat dried beans from the jar, and only look at ponds with a grown-up, staying back from deep water.

objects.text:
Robo's guesses
1. a baby fish?
2. a baby snake?
3. a little rock?

What they become
1. tadpole: a frog
2. caterpillar: a butterfly
3. bean seed: a bean plant

Frog
starts: egg in water
young: tadpole
metamorphosis

Butterfly
starts: egg on a leaf
young: caterpillar
complete metamorphosis

Bean plant
starts: seed in soil
young: small plant
no big change of shape
All living things: start life, grow, make young, and the cycle goes on.

do.text: Life Cycles
Welcome to my nature table by the pond! I found three mystery babies.
Mystery babies? Let me guess what they are.
Number one swims. That's a baby fish!
Number two is long and wiggly. A baby snake!
And number three doesn't move at all. It's a little rock.
I wrote my guesses on the before board.
Not even close! Let's watch them grow and see.
Here's our question. What will each baby become?
What will each baby become?
Fox, what is a life cycle?
A life cycle is how a living thing changes during its life.
life cycle
First, it starts life.
Then it grows bigger.
When it's grown up, it makes young of its own.
And those young start the whole cycle again!
Round and round, like a wheel. That's why it's called a cycle!
Every living thing has a life cycle. But each kind changes in its own way.
each kind changes in its own way
Let's build a wheel for each of our mystery babies.
Mystery baby number one lives in the pond. Let's start with a frog.
Adult frogs lay their eggs in water.
A clump of frog eggs is called frogspawn.
week 1: frogspawn
Each tiny dark dot is a baby frog growing inside clear jelly.
How long until they hatch?
About one to three weeks. Warm water makes them hatch faster.
Pop! Out comes a tadpole.
week 3: tadpole
tail to swim, gills to breathe
It swims with its tail, and breathes underwater with gills, like a fish.
Ha! So my guess was half right. It looks like a baby fish.
It looks like one, but it's really a baby frog! It eats tiny water plants and grows for weeks.
What will the tadpole grow next: back legs or front legs?
back legs or front legs?
think...
Back legs come first! The front legs grow a few weeks later.
week 8: back legs first
Now it's a froglet: four legs, and a tail that is shrinking away.
week 12: froglet
Its new lungs breathe air, so it can climb out of the water.
Fun fact: adult frogs breathe with lungs, and they take in air through their skin too.
fun fact
And finally, an adult frog, with no tail at all!
adult frog
For many frogs, egg to froglet takes about three or four months.
When the adult lays eggs in the water, the cycle starts again.
A big change of body shape like this has a name. Metamorphosis!
metamorphosis = a big change of body shape
Metamorphosis. Egg, tadpole, froglet, frog!
Mystery baby number two was the stripy caterpillar. Let's start with a monarch butterfly.
This plant is milkweed. A monarch lays her eggs on its leaves, one at a time.
milkweed
Here is her egg on a milkweed leaf. A real one is about as small as a pinhead.
day 1: egg on a milkweed leaf
About four days later, it hatches.
Out crawls a tiny caterpillar. Its first meal is usually its own eggshell!
day 4: caterpillar
Then it munches milkweed leaves, and grows, and grows.
It grows so fast that it sheds its tight skin, again and again.
Scientists call this stage the larva.
caterpillar = larva
So it's not a baby snake after all!
No way! It's a baby butterfly. Look at all its little feet.
After about two weeks, it hangs from a twig and sheds its skin one last time.
Now it's a chrysalis, green with gold dots. Its science name is pupa.
week 3: chrysalis (pupa)
Oh, I know this one! It's a cocoon!
Close, but no. A butterfly makes a chrysalis. A moth caterpillar spins a silk cocoon.
It looks still. But inside, the caterpillar's body is changing into a butterfly's body.
About ten days later, something comes out. What do you think it is?
What comes out?
think...
A butterfly! Its wings come out crumpled and wet.
week 4: adult butterfly
It pumps them open, lets them dry, and then it can fly.
Here's a surprise. A grown-up butterfly never grows any bigger.
adults don't grow bigger
It drinks nectar from flowers, and lays eggs on milkweed. The cycle starts again!
Egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, adult. Four stages that look completely different.
Four completely different stages is called complete metamorphosis.
complete metamorphosis: 4 different-looking stages
Time for the life cycle chant! Start and grow, make young and go.
Round and round the life cycle flows!
Now act it out! Curl up small, like an egg.
curl up!
Wiggle like a caterpillar!
wiggle!
Hold still like a chrysalis.
hold still...
Now open your arms wide, like a butterfly!
fly!
I say egg, you say caterpillar. Egg!
Egg!
Caterpillar!
Chrysalis!
Butterfly!
And mystery baby number three, my little rock?
It's a bean seed! A seed is how a bean plant's life starts.
seed
Let's cut one open and look inside.
Outside is the seed coat, a tough jacket that keeps it safe.
Inside is a tiny baby plant, already waiting.
And all this is stored food. It feeds the baby plant until it has leaves.
Give the seed water, air and warmth, and it sprouts. Scientists say it germinates.
germinate = sprout
What comes out first: the root or the shoot?
root or shoot?
think...
The root! It grows out first, and it grows down.
week 2: root first
Then the shoot pushes up toward the light.
then the shoot grows up
A seed doesn't need light to sprout. But the young plant needs light to grow.
sprouting: no light needed
growing: light needed
Leaves open, and the young plant grows taller every week.
week 4: young plant
I'll measure it. Then measure twice, just to be sure!
Next come little white flowers.
week 6: flowers
And the flowers become green bean pods.
pods
Open a pod and look. Inside are new bean seeds!
week 8: pods with seeds
For a bush bean, seed to new pods takes about two months.
At the end of the season, the old plant dries up and dies.
But its seeds can grow into new plants, so the cycle goes on.
A plant has a life cycle too! Seed, sprout, plant, flowers, pods.
Now we have three life-cycle wheels side by side. Let's compare them.
How does each one start? The frog starts as an egg in water.
The butterfly starts as an egg on a leaf.
And the bean starts as a seed in the soil.
Does the baby look like the grown-up?
Not for the frog. A tadpole looks nothing like a frog.
Not for the butterfly either. Caterpillar and butterfly look totally different.
The young bean plant looks partly like the grown one. It just has no flowers yet.
Frogs and butterflies change body shape: metamorphosis. A bean plant just grows and adds new parts.
Frogs and butterflies make young by laying eggs. The bean makes seeds in pods.
So here's the rule. All three start life, grow, make young, and the cycle goes on.
find the rule
Robots don't grow or have young. So we don't have a life cycle. We're not alive!
That's right, Robo. And you kids grow too, but you don't change shape like a tadpole!
Fun fact: some monarchs fly thousands of kilometres to spend the winter in Mexico.
fun fact
Start and grow, make young and go.
Round and round the life cycle flows!
Challenge time! What comes next? Number one: a tadpole with back legs.
think...
Front legs, and then it becomes a froglet!
Number two: a caterpillar. What comes next?
think...
A chrysalis!
Number three: flowers on a bean plant. What comes next?
think...
Pods with new seeds inside!
Number four is mine. Butterfly order: egg, chrysalis, caterpillar, adult.
Is Robo right? Can you fix it?
think...
The caterpillar comes before the chrysalis. Egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, adult!
Last one. Which of our three does not go through metamorphosis?
think...
The bean plant! It grows bigger, but it never changes body shape.
Quick quiz! One: where does a frog lay its eggs?
think...
In water!
Two: what stage comes between caterpillar and butterfly?
think...
The chrysalis, also called the pupa.
Three: what grows out of a bean seed first?
think...
The root!
Four: name one thing all three life cycles share.
think...
They all start life, grow, make young, and the cycle goes on.
Five: does a caterpillar turn into a butterfly inside a cocoon?
think...
No! Butterflies make a chrysalis. Moths spin cocoons.
Time to fix my before board. Here is the after board!
Frog: egg, tadpole, froglet, adult. Butterfly: egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, adult.
Bean: seed, sprout, plant, flowers, and pods full of new seeds.
Try a bean in a jar at home, with a grown-up. Watch the root come out first!
Watched it, measured it, learned it!
Bye for now, friends!
